roots.title: Crawler Engine
roots.note: news-crawler-itself: fetch loop, worker-thread compression, remote runtime
detail: Cycle 73 (2026-07-22, Sonnet 5 after a mid-loop model swap) moved the entire crawler engine out of copilot-dl-news into the sibling package news-crawler-itself — 17 files + 4 config JSONs — after discovering the extraction playbook's own file list was missing 5 of 12 required files (hash-manifest.js, resource-shield.js, intelligence-pool.js, export-retention.js, orchestrator-utils.js), found only by tracing the real require graphs.

The same cycle shipped a new GzipPool over worker_threads (pool size min(cpus-1,4), ArrayBuffer transfer, respawn-once-then-dead policy) replacing synchronous zlib.gzipSync in the fetch loop; two real bugs were self-caught pre-ship — a queued-job-forever hang in close() and a spawnSync event-loop deadlock where a fixture HTTP server in the same process could never answer the child (banked as a permanent memory rule: async spawn for integration tests).

Deployed to the Oracle box with buildId change + PM2 0-restarts, then DB-evidence-verified: ~83-87% real compression on live bbc.com/theguardian.com/apnews.com content and intact 1s-floor politeness (median ~1.04s deltas); reuters.com hit a genuine external 401 bot-block, npr.org honestly reported as 0-yield.

Standalone test count landed at 45/45 including 2 end-to-end integration tests through the actual child-process entry point; a 948-test broader sweep confirmed the 40 pre-existing failures were unrelated to the extraction.

An earlier Oracle deploy (cycle 70) was only rescued by DB evidence: a false "deploy complete" was caught and the entire D2a robots/crawl-delay politeness layer turned out to be dead code on the remote worker (grep: 0 matches) — fixed with polite-fetch.js which gates EVERY redirect hop with redirect:'manual'.

Phase E of cycle 73 overran: the "5 sites x 10 pages" owner test crawl ran far past target across PM2 restarts before cycle 73.5 caught it, and it exposed that run-worker.js is one-shot so PM2 fork_mode autorestart cycles it on every clean completion — worker restart count is NOT a crash signal; as of 2026-07-27 the whole package still has no .git (owner decision pending).

roots.title: Politeness Stack
roots.note: robots floors + 429 backoff escalation; 0×429 across 3,419 live responses
detail: The safety-evidence headline number: 3,419 live responses across 7 mixed hosts at concurrency 3 with 0x429, 0x403, 0x503 — and the agent self-caught an incoherence where its earlier proposal quoted a 3.23x speedup at concurrency 4 next to safety data gathered at concurrency 3, so it re-measured at the same concurrency before recommending anything.

Default worker concurrency is pinned at 3 (4 bought only +12% throughput for 33% more per-host load), with a guard test asserting the default so a silent revert fails CI, and the setting is a GATED owner directive checked by tools/dev/checks/ritual-compliance.check.js.

Guardian's ~31-34s inter-fetch gap was mis-read as whole-process dead-time for ~3 months before tools/crawl/host-health.js made the distinction legible — it classifies hosts FAST / POLITE-THROTTLE / SLOW-IRREGULAR by gap regularity (coefficient of variation), proving the gap was a compliant robots crawl-delay floor in limiter.js, not a bug.

The real throughput lever (task #45) is scheduling AROUND crawl-delays, not shrinking them: seed more hosts and release/refill a throttled host's worker slot so its polite idle overlaps other hosts' fetches; per-host history sizes the lease so a slow-delay host is never over-leased.

Cycle 120's owner-directed run delivered 2,167 pages (2,069 HTTP 200s, 696.1 MB at 495 KB/s avg) with zero 429s across all 10 hosts — recorded in the cycle stanza literally as result "OWNER_ASK_DELIVERED_2167_pages_0x429".

A planned second Oracle crawl node was analyzed and rejected: under a shared host's crawl-delay-sum constraint a second node adds ZERO throughput to that host while costing WAN RTT per fetch, and per-process 429 backoff is invisible cross-node — the one safety-critical missing piece for distribution.

A frontier-fill busy-loop once DoS'd the electron server (tasks #37-#40): concurrent frontier reconciliation on synchronous better-sqlite3 starved the HTTP event loop — port REFUSED while the pid stayed alive and workers kept downloading; the true fix moved reconcile/hydration off the crawl thread (dispatch-and-return).

Per memory, frontier-seeded crawls of URLs-without-content gave a 6x yield improvement over discovery crawling (task #35), and hubFraction is now tunable per-request on POST /frontier/hydrate (clamped 0..1, live-verified at 0.2).

roots.title: News Database
roots.note: ncdb unified layer over a ~30 GB archive; 16.9k pages crawled during cycles
detail: The owner-approved dedup (2026-07-27, copy→dedup→verify→swap on the live archive) shrank http_responses 325,614 → 290,144 (−35,470 redundant rows), removed 10,537 content_storage and 4,829 content_analysis rows, collapsed 25,351 duplicate groups to 0, and cut the file 30.24 → 28.89 GB with 0 unique content lost — distinct content sha 186,255 and analyzed sha 70,907 both unchanged, foreign_key_check=0, integrity_check=ok.

The dedup's hidden trap was article_place_relations, a reverse-FK child with ON DELETE CASCADE that a naive delete would have silently destroyed — found only by scanning the FULL reverse-FK graph and re-pointing cascade children to the keeper row; post-swap a real crawl added +37 rows with dup_groups staying at 0.

The WAL incident (2026-07-20): an unbounded inline probe of a known-slow query against the then-29GB DB hit synchronous better-sqlite3 native code that no in-process timeout can interrupt; the Bash timeout killed the shell but not the node grandchild, which ground on as an orphan for 25+ minutes pinning the WAL snapshot — news.db-wal ballooned to 870MB while the app kept writing.

Prevention shipped as tools/db/timed-probe.js: child-process execution with a hard external kill at --timeout-ms, a LIMIT guard that REFUSES unbounded SQL (the incident query exits code 3), and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN printed BEFORE timing so the diagnostic survives a kill; verified live — bounded probe 1ms, the full incident query killed at exactly 20s with zero orphans.

The incident's diagnostic yield beat its cost: the slow query's real killer wasn't the 2-table COALESCE sort (~1.5s) but a per-row correlated scalar subquery (MAX(analysis_version)) over 1.68M rows under a TEMP B-TREE sort; the follow-up --fast variant ran in 5ms vs killed-at-60s.

A planner gotcha lives in memory: the recent-headlines query picks idx_classification (~all rows) plus a TEMP B-TREE sort (~4s) unless pinned with INDEXED BY idx_content_analysis_analyzed_at (~1ms), and fetched_at/analyzed_at mix ISO-T-Z and space-form timestamps so every comparison must wrap datetime() on both sides.

detail: NOT a duplicate of the factory's TF-PROBES, though the 2026-07-30 review flagged the pair as near-identical — this differentiation is the answer: TR-PROBES is the CONVENTION (a durable claim ships with a runnable re-verification, and orient cannot pass while one is red), TF-PROBES is the TOOL FAMILY that implements it (run-probes.js plus the check scripts, counted in the factory inventory). roots.title: DB Safety Kit

detail: tools/db is 12 scripts; the two with war stories are timed-probe.js and dedup-http-responses.js, guarding a live 28 GB news.db.

timed-probe.js exists because an inline slow-query probe against live news.db once left an uninterruptible better-sqlite3 call in an orphaned grandchild process that pinned an 870 MB WAL file — the tool now runs every query under an external-kill watchdog with a mandatory LIMIT guard and plan-before-timing.

The guard is itself probed: the timed-probe-guard orient probe feeds it 'SELECT 1 FROM urls' with no LIMIT and asserts it refuses with exit code 3, so a refactor can't silently delete the incident protection.

dedup-http-responses.js ran an owner-approved copy→dedup→verify→swap on the live DB, shrinking http_responses 325,614→290,144 rows with zero unique content lost — losslessness verified by sha-based invariants, not content_id.

The dedup nearly destroyed data via a hidden trap: article_place_relations had an ON DELETE CASCADE foreign key that a naive delete would have cascaded through — the fix scanned the FULL reverse-FK graph and re-pointed CASCADE children to the keeper row before deleting, then ran foreign_key_check + integrity_check post-swap.

Post-swap, the freshly written multi-GB DB opened so slowly cold that the 60-second electron startup probe failed — a retry once the OS cache was warm succeeded, a false-corruption scare now recorded as a known gotcha.

techs.title: Frontier Headline Quality II
techs.research: push real-headline yield further via shape preference + host density
detail: Delivered cycle 167 (2026-08-02) — round three found the binding constraint was PATH DEPTH, a shape the first two rounds never sampled. `isArticleShapedUrl` opened with a blanket `segs.length < 2` reject, so FLAT-SLUG newsrooms were structurally invisible: measured against 120,000 already-fetched titles, 0 of 2,443 path-depth-1 rows were admitted — businessinsider.com (112 real headlines), france24 webdoc/graphics, liberties.aljazeera.com, politico.eu, newsweek, timesofisrael, straitstimes, apnews. The loss hit BOTH consumers of the predicate, so already-crawled depth-1 stories were also being filtered out of the /api/v1/crawl/articles product listing, not just skipped by frontier selection.

The fix admits depth-1 only on a strong slug signal — 6+ hyphen parts, deliberately STRICTER than the 4 accepted at depth>=2 because a flat path carries no section context to disambiguate. Measured old-vs-new over 200,000 live frontier URLs: 1,462 GAINED, 0 LOST, and every gain at depth 1 — monotonic by measurement, not by argument. On the fetched-title ground truth it admits 178 rows at 98.3% precision (163 headlines of >=6 words, 12 of 4-5, 3 non-articles: two POLITICO special reports and one Atlantic privacy page). Section landings (/markets, /news, /video, /world-markets) carry 1-3 hyphen parts and stay rejected; 5 parts is below the depth-1 bar even though it clears the depth>=2 one.

Second defect found in passing and fixed: tools/dev-bridge/checks/report-fresh-headlines.js carried an INLINE COPY of the predicate whose comment claimed it mirrored ArticleSignalsService. Measured, it did not — the copy predated every cycle-75 fix (trailing-slash strip, media/hub vetoes, CMS /articles/<id>, live-blog fragments), so the owner's headline report was applying a two-rounds-stale filter. Its 'dependency-free' justification did not survive contact either: the file already requires better-sqlite3. Now one predicate in one place.

Round one (cycle 50) proved the binding constraint was hub-domination, not URL shape: shape preference alone still yielded "Society"/"Education" section titles because requeuedHubs=6/6; the hubFraction cap (0.5) + hub-backfill was the real lever, and the acceptance test flipped from section titles to real headlines in one live crawl (~56 pages).

Round two (cycle 75) hardened the predicate itself on 1,800 real DB URLs — recovering 136 under-selected articles and rejecting 33 live-blog pagination fragments — with an adversarial 3-skeptic review refuting the first fix twice on multi-word section-hub landings the stratified sample had missed (apnews /hub/us-department-of-education vs the control /hub/congress).

Cycle 77 established the measure-before-build precedent this node inherits: the recommended url-intelligence negative veto was measured redundant on a 5,000-URL real frontier sample, and the shipped alternative — a frontier-composition report tool (label distribution × copilot-admit overlap × cross-host share-junk count, WAL-safe via timed-probe) — is the instrument any further headline push should read first.

The other proven quality levers already exist to combine: host-density ranking (frontier-hosts.js, necessary-but-not-sufficient per the frontier-leak memory), the article-new quality gate + yield filter (default 0.6 keeps nytimes at 84% yield; strict 0.9 excludes it and backfills cnn/scmp), and per-request hubFraction tuning on /frontier/hydrate.

Known residual junk source: cross-host social-share links pollute discovery, but cycle 79 proved they CANNOT be filtered at discovery time — news-db-analysis's GraphAccess interface explicitly consumes cross-host edges, so the filter must live at selection, not storage. This row read "~16k" until cycle 167 re-ran the instrument and measured 24,997 — the count is GROWING, which is what the tool was built to make visible. It is dead weight in the table, not a yield drag: selectDueFrontier is host-scoped, so these rows are never crawled. Deleting them is an owner-gated live-DB write.

Still open after cycle 167 (the depth-1 fix did not touch these): a distinct yield loss where nytimes.com articles store their title as the bare string "nytimes.com" — a fetch/paywall artifact, not a selection problem, so it needs the extraction path rather than this predicate. And the depth-1 gate buys precision with recall: single-segment stories carrying fewer than 6 hyphen parts stay rejected, which is the deliberate trade, not an oversight.

'Rename X to Y', 'restructure A as B' style suggestions are inadmissible unless tied to a measured axis, because preference-shaped changes are exactly the ones that flip back.

REVERSAL CHECK before proposing: search the ledger for the same surface. If a prior cycle moved it in the OPPOSITE direction, the suggestion is REJECTED as oscillation — unless the evidence shows the prior direction was measured wrong, in which case it is a CORRECTION and must say so in those words. The ledger is the memory that makes back-and-forth detectable.

THE FIXED POINT IS A VALID ANSWER: this review may return 'no improvements above the bar' — that IS the fully-improved state for now, recorded in the REVIEW LOG as a convergence datum, and it costs one honest sentence instead of an invented task. A review that must always produce suggestions will eventually produce busy work by construction.

DECLINED IS RECORDED: every suggestion considered and rejected goes in the REVIEW LOG with its reason, so the next run does not re-derive or re-propose it. Nothing evaporates; nothing loops.

The ledger is the memory that makes back-and-forth detectable.

THE FIXED POINT IS A VALID ANSWER: this review may return 'no improvements above the bar' — that IS the fully-improved state for now, recorded in the REVIEW LOG as a convergence datum, and it costs one honest sentence instead of an invented task. A review that must always produce suggestions will eventually produce busy work by construction.

BUSY-WORK SELF-CHECK before executing any accepted suggestion: run churn-scan (RB-004) on the target files — a target that keeps being 'improved' is a red flag; check the workflow scorecard's cost-to-catch; and if the last two runs of this review produced work whose measured axes did not move, the review must SAY it is idling and pick a materially different lane (a gated decision to surface, a measurement to build, or nothing).
DECLINED IS RECORDED: every suggestion considered and rejected goes in the REVIEW LOG with its reason, so the next run does not re-derive or re-propose it. Nothing evaporates; nothing loops.

Candidate measured axes for the CRAWLER (seed list, extend per run): ncdb-debt (raw SQL outside ncdb — the founding ratchet, currently guarded at 241), event-loop starvation incidents (the c39/c40 class), zombie-state classes without a corroborated transition (the c150 class), per-host politeness overhead vs measured throughput (the c45 scheduling lever), reconciliation blind spots (the redirect_chain class), deploy-gate false-positive rate.
